Curitiba is in the state of Paraná. The city's modern identity is closely associated with public transport, pedestrian areas, parks and thoughtfully designed public spaces.

For a first visit, explore its central streets and principal architectural landmarks: Rua das Flores, Nossa Senhora da Luz Cathedral, Rua 24 Horas, Ópera de Arame and the Oscar Niemeyer Museum.

Curitiba works well as a city stop in its own right in southern Brazil, or as part of a longer journey that also takes in Florianópolis and Porto Alegre.

Cusco was the capital of the Inca Empire. The city retains a distinctive blend of Inca and Spanish architecture: many colonial-era buildings were erected on the sites of earlier religious and administrative structures.

A city itinerary can include Plaza de Armas, Qorikancha, the Church of Santo Domingo, cathedrals, palaces and museums. Another aspect of the visit is the local market, with handicrafts and goods made from llama and alpaca wool.

The area around Cusco extends this historical journey. Sacsayhuamán, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu are usually the principal stops in this region.

Cuverville Island lies in the northern part of the Errera Channel, off the Antarctic Peninsula. The steep-sided island rises above a rocky shore, surrounded by drifting ice floes and icebergs. A large colony of gentoo penguins inhabits its snow-free areas.

Penguins constantly move between the colony and the sea. Glaciers and neighbouring mountains are visible from the shore, while traces of the area's whaling past remain near the landing site. Walks are led by the expedition team, taking account of the routes the birds use to reach the water.
